answer: Plant each identity as one tree in a shared orchard grove: joining requires staking a bond that grows like a tree, with a pigment tag burned into the ledger marking its lineage. Each epoch, a random audit samples one grove branch and demands fresh proof of useful work; a clone's tag matches its siblings, so one failed audit burns the whole grove's bond. An attacker must therefore fund and tend a separate, verifiably distinct orchard for every fake, paying the full bond and work cost per identity, while honest agents tend just one tree.
